sanskrit: māgadhasya punaḥ putraṃ hatvā ṣaḍbhir ajihmagaiḥ sāśvaṃ sasūtaṃ taruṇam aśvaketum apātayat
english: Then, slaying with six straight-flying arrows the youthful son of the Māgadha king, Aśvaketu, he brought him down together with his horses and his charioteer.

sanskrit: mārtikāvatakaṃ bhojaṃ tataḥ kuñjaraketanam kṣurapreṇa samunmathya nanāda visṛjañ śarān
english: Then with a razor-edged shaft he hewed down the Bhoja of Mārtikāvata, whose banner bore an elephant, and roared aloud as he loosed his arrows.

sanskrit: tasya dauḥśāsanir viddhvā caturbhiś caturo hayān sūtam ekena vivyādha daśabhiś cārjunātmajam
english: Then the son of Duḥśāsana pierced his four horses with four shafts, struck his charioteer with one, and the son of Arjuna with ten.

sanskrit: tato dauḥśāsaniṃ kārṣṇir viddhvā saptabhir āśugaiḥ saṃrambhād raktanayano vākyam uccair athābravīt
english: Then the son of Kṛṣṇā's lord, having pierced the son of Duḥśāsana with seven swift arrows, his eyes red with fury, spoke aloud these words:

sanskrit: pitā tavāhavaṃ tyaktvā gataḥ kāpuruṣo yathā diṣṭyā tvam api jānīṣe yoddhuṃ na tv adya mokṣyase
english: "Your father has fled the battle and gone away like a coward; by good fortune you too know how to fight—yet today you shall not escape."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ karmāraparimārjitam nārācaṃ visasarjāsmai taṃ drauṇis tribhir ācchinat
english: Having spoken these words, he loosed at him an iron shaft burnished by the smith; but the son of Droṇa cut it apart with three arrows.

sanskrit: tasyārjunir dhvajaṃ chittvā śalyaṃ tribhir atāḍayat taṃ śalyo navabhir bāṇair gārdhrapatrair atāḍayat
english: The son of Arjuna, having cut down his banner, struck Śalya with three shafts; and Śalya struck him in turn with nine vulture-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: tasyārjunir dhvajaṃ chittvā ubhau ca pārṣṇisārathī taṃ vivyādhāyasaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ so 'pakrāmad rathāntaram
english: The son of Arjuna cut down his banner and both his flanking charioteers, and pierced him with six iron shafts, so that he withdrew to another chariot.

sanskrit: śatruṃjayaṃ candraketuṃ meghavegaṃ suvarcasam sūryabhāsaṃ ca pañcaitān hatvā vivyādha saubalam
english: Having slain these five—Śatruṃjaya, Candraketu, Meghavega, Suvarcas, and Sūryabhāsa—he pierced the son of Subala.

sanskrit: taṃ saubalas tribhir viddhvā duryodhanam athābravīt sarva enaṃ pramathnīmaḥ puraikaikaṃ hinasti naḥ
english: Subala's son, having pierced him with three shafts, then said to Duryodhana: "Let us all crush him together, before he destroys us one by one."

sanskrit: athābravīt tadā droṇaṃ karṇo vaikartano vṛṣā purā sarvān pramathnāti brūhy asya vadham āśu naḥ
english: Then Karṇa Vaikartana, the bull among men, said to Droṇa: "Before he crushes us all, tell us quickly the means of his slaying."

sanskrit: tato droṇo maheṣvāsaḥ sarvāṃs tān pratyabhāṣata asti vo 'syāntaraṃ kaś cit kumārasya prapaśyati
english: Then Droṇa, the mighty archer, answered them all: "Does any one of you perceive a single flaw in this youth?

sanskrit: anv asya pitaraṃ hy adya carataḥ sarvatodiśam śīghratāṃ narasiṃhasya pāṇḍaveyasya paśyata
english: "Behold today the swiftness of this lion among men, this scion of Pāṇḍu, who ranges in every direction even as his father does.

sanskrit: dhanurmaṇḍalam evāsya rathamārgeṣu dṛśyate saṃdadhānasya viśikhāñ śīghraṃ caiva vimuñcataḥ
english: "Along the courses of his chariot only the circle of his bow is seen, as he nocks his shafts and looses them with speed.

sanskrit: ārujann iva me prāṇān mohayann api sāyakaiḥ praharṣayati mā bhūyaḥ saubhadraḥ paravīrahā
english: "Though he wrenches at my very life-breath and bewilders me with his shafts, this son of Subhadrā, slayer of enemy heroes, gladdens me all the more.

sanskrit: ati mā nandayaty eṣa saubhadro vicaran raṇe antaraṃ yasya saṃrabdhā na paśyanti mahārathāḥ
english: "This son of Subhadrā delights me beyond measure as he ranges through the battle—he whose flaw the furious great car-warriors cannot find.

sanskrit: asyato laghuhastasya diśaḥ sarvā maheṣubhiḥ na viśeṣaṃ prapaśyāmi raṇe gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ
english: "As he shoots his great arrows light-handed in every direction, I can see no difference in battle between him and the wielder of Gāṇḍīva."

sanskrit: atha karṇaḥ punar droṇam āhārjuniśarārditaḥ sthātavyam iti tiṣṭhāmi pīḍyamāno 'bhimanyunā
english: Then Karṇa, tormented by the arrows of Arjuna's son, said again to Droṇa: "I hold my ground only because I must, though I am sorely pressed by Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: tejasvinaḥ kumārasya śarāḥ paramadāruṇāḥ kṣiṇvanti hṛdayaṃ me 'dya ghorāḥ pāvakatejasaḥ
english: "The arrows of this fiery youth, most terrible, dreadful, blazing like fire, today waste away my very heart."

sanskrit: tam ācāryo 'bravīt karṇaṃ śanakaiḥ prahasann iva abhedyam asya kavacaṃ yuvā cāśuparākramaḥ
english: To this the preceptor said softly to Karṇa, as if with a smile: "His armor cannot be pierced, and the youth is swift in valor.

sanskrit: upadiṣṭā mayā asya pituḥ kavacadhāraṇā tām eṣa nikhilāṃ vetti dhruvaṃ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: "The wearing of armor was taught by me to his father, and this conqueror of hostile cities knows it surely in its entirety.

sanskrit: śakyaṃ tv asya dhanuś chettuṃ jyāṃ ca bāṇaiḥ samāhitaiḥ abhīśavo hayāś caiva tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī
english: "Yet his bow can be cut, and his bowstring too, with well-aimed arrows—and likewise his reins, his horses, and both his flanking charioteers.

sanskrit: etat kuru maheṣvāsa rādheya yadi śakyate athainaṃ vimukhīkṛtya paścāt praharaṇaṃ kuru
english: "Do this, O mighty archer, son of Rādhā, if it can be done; then, having turned him away, strike him afterward.

sanskrit: sadhanuṣko na śakyo 'yam api jetuṃ surāsuraiḥ virathaṃ vidhanuṣkaṃ ca kuruṣvainaṃ yadīcchasi
english: "While he holds his bow, not even the gods and demons together could vanquish him; so, if you wish, make him chariotless and bowless."

sanskrit: tad ācāryavacaḥ śrutvā karṇo vaikartanas tvaran asyato laghuhastasya pṛṣatkair dhanur ācchinat
english: Hearing the preceptor's word, Karṇa Vaikartana made haste, and with his shafts cut the bow of the light-handed archer as he shot.

sanskrit: aśvān asyāvadhīd bhojo gautamaḥ pārṣṇisārathī śeṣās tu chinnadhanvānaṃ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: The Bhoja slew his horses, Gautama his flanking charioteer, while the rest, his bow now severed, overwhelmed him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tvaramāṇās tvarākāle virathaṃ ṣaṇ mahārathāḥ śaravarṣair akaruṇā bālam ekam avākiran
english: Hastening in the hour of haste, six great car-warriors, pitiless, overwhelmed with showers of arrows that one boy, now chariotless.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā virathaḥ svadharmam anupālayan khaḍgacarmadharaḥ śrīmān utpapāta vihāyasam
english: His bow cut, his chariot gone, yet upholding his own warrior's duty, the illustrious one, bearing sword and shield, leaped up into the sky.

sanskrit: mārgaiḥ sa kaiśikādyaiś ca lāghavena balena ca ārjunir vyacarad vyomni bhṛśaṃ vai pakṣirāḍ iva
english: With the gliding maneuvers called kaiśika and the rest, with lightness and with strength, the son of Arjuna ranged the heavens, much like the king of birds.

sanskrit: mayy eva nipataty eṣa sāsir ity ūrdhvadṛṣṭayaḥ vivyadhus taṃ maheṣvāsāḥ samare chidradarśinaḥ
english: "He is falling upon me, sword in hand!"—thus with upturned gaze the mighty archers, watching for an opening in the fight, pierced him.

sanskrit: tasya droṇo 'cchinan muṣṭau khaḍgaṃ maṇimayatsarum rādheyo niśitair bāṇair vyadhamac carma cottamam
english: Droṇa cut off, at the hilt, his sword with its jewel-studded pommel, and the son of Rādhā shattered with his sharp arrows that excellent shield.

sanskrit: vyasicarmeṣupūrṇāṅgaḥ so 'ntarikṣāt punaḥ kṣitim āsthitaś cakram udyamya droṇaṃ kruddho 'bhyadhāvata
english: Bereft of sword and shield, his limbs full of arrows, he came down again from the sky to the earth, and lifting up a chariot-wheel, in his wrath he rushed upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: sa cakrareṇūjjvalaśobhitāṅgo; babhāv atīvonnatacakrapāṇiḥ raṇe 'bhimanyuḥ kṣaṇadāsubhadraḥ; sa vāsubhadrānukṛtiṃ prakurvan
english: His limbs shining bright with the dust of the wheel, his wheel-bearing arm raised high, Abhimanyu, that night-born son of Subhadrā, blazed in the battle, imitating the very likeness of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: srutarudhirakṛtaikarāgavaktro; bhrukuṭipuṭākuṭilo 'tisiṃhanādaḥ prabhur amitabalo raṇe 'bhimanyur; nṛpavaramadhyagato bhṛśaṃ vyarājat
english: His face dyed a single hue by the streaming blood, his brow knit and crooked with frowning, roaring like a great lion—the lord Abhimanyu of measureless strength shone resplendent in battle, set amid the foremost of kings.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca viṣṇoḥ svasānandikaraḥ sa viṣṇvāyudhabhūṣitaḥ rarājātirathaḥ saṃkhye janārdana ivāparaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: That peerless car-warrior, the joy of Viṣṇu's sister, adorned with the weapon of Viṣṇu, shone in the battle like a second Janārdana.

sanskrit: mārutoddhūtakeśāntam udyatārivarāyudham vapuḥ samīkṣya pṛthvīśā duḥsamīkṣyaṃ surair api
english: The lords of earth beheld his form—the ends of his hair tossed by the wind, his fine weapon raised against his foes—a form hard to look upon even for the gods.

sanskrit: tac cakraṃ bhṛśam udvignāḥ saṃcicchidur anekadhā mahārathas tataḥ kārṣṇiḥ saṃjagrāha mahāgadām
english: Sorely alarmed, they cut that wheel apart in many pieces; then the great car-warrior, the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, seized a great mace.

sanskrit: vidhanuḥsyandanāsis tair vicakraś cāribhiḥ kṛtaḥ abhimanyur gadāpāṇir aśvatthāmānam ādravat
english: Stripped by those foes of bow, chariot, and sword, and made wheelless as well, Abhimanyu, mace in hand, rushed upon Aśvatthāman.

sanskrit: sa gadām udyatāṃ dṛṣṭvā jvalantīm aśanīm iva apākrāmad rathopasthād vikramāṃs trīn nararṣabhaḥ
english: Seeing that uplifted mace blazing like a thunderbolt, that bull among men sprang from the floor of his chariot, taking three strides away.

sanskrit: tasyāśvān gadayā hatvā tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī śarācitāṅgaḥ saubhadraḥ śvāvidvat pratyadṛśyata
english: Having slain with his mace that one's horses and both his flanking charioteers, the son of Subhadrā, his body bristling with arrows, appeared like a porcupine.

sanskrit: tataḥ subaladāyādaṃ kālakeyam apothayat jaghāna cāsyānucarān gāndhārān saptasaptatim
english: Then he crushed Kālakeya, the heir of Subala, and slew his followers, seventy and seven Gāndhāras.

sanskrit: punar brahmavasātīyāñ jaghāna rathino daśa kekayānāṃ rathān sapta hatvā ca daśa kuñjarān dauḥśāsanirathaṃ sāśvaṃ gadayā samapothayat
english: Again he slew ten chariot-warriors of the Brahmavasātīyas, and having destroyed seven chariots of the Kekayas and ten elephants, he crushed with his mace the chariot of Duḥśāsana's son together with its horses.

sanskrit: tato dauḥśāsaniḥ kruddho gadām udyamya māriṣa abhidudrāva saubhadraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Then the son of Duḥśāsana, enraged, O lord, raised his mace and rushed at the son of Subhadrā, crying, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: tāv udyatagadau vīrāv anyonyavadhakāṅkṣiṇau bhrātṛvyau saṃprajahrāte pureva tryambakāntakau
english: Those two heroes, their maces upraised, each longing to slay the other—cousins both—fell upon one another like Tryambaka and the Ender of old.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ gadāgrābhyāṃ saṃhatya patitau kṣitau indradhvajāv ivotsṛṣṭau raṇamadhye paraṃtapau
english: Smiting each other with the heads of their maces, those two scorchers of foes fell to the ground in the midst of the battle, like two banners of Indra cast down.

sanskrit: dauḥśāsanir athotthāya kurūṇāṃ kīrtivardhanaḥ prottiṣṭhamānaṃ saubhadraṃ gadayā mūrdhny atāḍayat
english: Then the son of Duḥśāsana, that enhancer of the Kurus' fame, rose up first, and struck the son of Subhadrā upon the head with his mace as he was rising.

sanskrit: gadāvegena mahatā vyāyāmena ca mohitaḥ vicetā nyapatad bhūmau saubhadraḥ paravīrahā evaṃ vinihato rājann eko bahubhir āhave
english: Stunned by the great force of the mace and by his own exertion, the son of Subhadrā, slayer of enemy heroes, fell senseless to the earth. Thus, O king, was he slain—one against many in the battle.

sanskrit: kṣobhayitvā camūṃ sarvāṃ nalinīm iva kuñjaraḥ aśobhata hato vīro vyādhair vanagajo yathā
english: Having shaken the whole host as an elephant churns a lotus-pond, the slain hero shone even in death, like a wild elephant brought down by hunters.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā patitaṃ śūraṃ tāvakāḥ paryavārayan dāvaṃ dagdhvā yathā śāntaṃ pāvakaṃ śiśirātyaye
english: As that hero lay thus fallen, your warriors surrounded him, as men gather round a fire grown calm at winter's end after it has burned the forest.

sanskrit: vimṛdya taruśṛṅgāṇi saṃnivṛttam ivānilam astaṃ gatam ivādityaṃ taptvā bhāratavāhinīm
english: He was like the wind grown still after crushing the crowns of trees, like the sun gone to its setting after scorching the host of the Bhāratas;

sanskrit: upaplutaṃ yathā somaṃ saṃśuṣkam iva sāgaram pūrṇacandrābhavadanaṃ kākapakṣavṛtākṣakam
english: like the moon overtaken by eclipse, like an ocean run dry—he whose face was as the full moon, whose eyes were framed by curling side-locks.

sanskrit: taṃ bhūmau patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tāvakās te mahārathāḥ mudā paramayā yuktāś cukruśuḥ siṃhavan muhuḥ
english: Beholding him fallen to the earth, your great car-warriors, filled with the highest joy, again and again roared aloud like lions.

sanskrit: āsīt paramako harṣas tāvakānāṃ viśāṃ pate itareṣāṃ tu vīrāṇāṃ netrebhyaḥ prāpataj jalam
english: Supreme was the gladness of your men, O lord of peoples; but from the eyes of the other heroes the tears came falling down.

sanskrit: abhikrośanti bhūtāni antarikṣe viśāṃ pate dṛṣṭvā nipatitaṃ vīraṃ cyutaṃ candram ivāmbarāt
english: The beings in the sky cried out in lamentation, O lord of peoples, beholding the hero fallen, like the moon dropped from the firmament.

sanskrit: droṇakarṇamukhaiḥ ṣaḍbhir dhārtarāṣṭrair mahārathaiḥ eko 'yaṃ nihataḥ śete naiṣa dharmo mato hi naḥ
english: "By six great car-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's side, led by Droṇa and Karṇa, this one alone has been slain and now lies dead—this we do not hold to be righteous."

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate vīre bahv aśobhata medinī dyaur yathā pūrṇacandreṇa nakṣatragaṇamālinī
english: When that hero was slain, the earth shone richly forth, even as the heavens, garlanded with their throng of stars, shine with the full moon.

sanskrit: rukmapuṅkhaiś ca saṃpūrṇā rudhiraughapariplutā uttamāṅgaiś ca vīrāṇāṃ bhrājamānaiḥ sakuṇḍalaiḥ
english: It was strewn full with gold-nocked arrows, awash with floods of blood, and with the gleaming heads of heroes still wearing their earrings;

sanskrit: vicitraiś ca paristomaiḥ patākābhiś ca saṃvṛtā cāmaraiś ca kuthābhiś ca praviddhaiś cāmbarottamaiḥ
english: covered with many-hued saddle-cloths and with banners, with yak-tail fans and elephant-housings, and with scattered raiment of the finest sort;

sanskrit: rathāśvanaranāgānām alaṃkāraiś ca suprabhaiḥ khaḍgaiś ca niśitaiḥ pītair nirmuktair bhujagair iva
english: with the bright ornaments of chariots, horses, men, and elephants, and with sharp, burnished swords cast loose like serpents from their sloughs.

sanskrit: cāpaiś ca viśikhaiś chinnaiḥ śaktyṛṣṭiprāsakampanaiḥ vividhair āyudhaiś cānyaiḥ saṃvṛtā bhūr aśobhata
english: Strewn with bows and broken arrows, with lances, javelins, darts, and battle-staves, and with many other weapons of every kind, the earth shone resplendent.

sanskrit: vājibhiś cāpi nirjīvaiḥ svapadbhiḥ śoṇitokṣitaiḥ sārohair viṣamā bhūmiḥ saubhadreṇa nipātitaiḥ
english: With lifeless horses, fair of limb and drenched in blood, brought down with their riders by the son of Subhadrā, the ground was made rugged;

sanskrit: sāṅkuśaiḥ samahāmātraiḥ savarmāyudhaketubhiḥ parvatair iva vidhvastair viśikhonmathitair gajaiḥ
english: with elephants—their goads and their drivers, their armor, weapons, and standards with them—shattered like mountains and crushed by his arrows;

sanskrit: pṛthivyām anukīrṇaiś ca vyaśvasārathiyodhibhiḥ hradair iva prakṣubhitair hatanāgai rathottamaiḥ
english: and with foremost chariots strewn upon the ground, their horses, charioteers, and warriors gone, their elephants slain—like lakes whipped into turmoil.

sanskrit: padātisaṃghaiś ca hatair vividhāyudhabhūṣaṇaiḥ bhīrūṇāṃ trāsajananī ghorarūpābhavan mahī
english: With slain bands of foot-soldiers, adorned with weapons of every kind, the earth became a thing of dreadful aspect, begetting terror in the timid.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ bhūmau candrārkasadṛśadyutim tāvakānāṃ parā prītiḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ cābhavad vyathā
english: Seeing him fallen to the earth, him whose splendor was like the sun and the moon, supreme was the gladness of your men, and grief was upon the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: abhimanyau hate rājañ śiśuke 'prāptayauvane saṃprādravac camūḥ sarvā dharmarājasya paśyataḥ
english: When Abhimanyu was slain, O king—a child not yet come to his youth—the whole host fled in rout before the very eyes of the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: dīryamāṇaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā saubhadre vinipātite ajātaśatruḥ svān vīrān idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing his army breaking apart now that the son of Subhadrā was struck down, Ajātaśatru spoke these words to his heroes:

sanskrit: svargam eṣa gataḥ śūro yo hato naparāṅmukhaḥ saṃstambhayata mā bhaiṣṭa vijeṣyāmo raṇe ripūn
english: "This hero, slain with his face never turned away, has gone to heaven. Stand firm; fear not; we shall yet conquer our foes in the field."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ sa mahātejā duḥkhitebhyo mahādyutiḥ dharmarājo yudhāṃ śreṣṭho bruvan duḥkham apānudat
english: Thus that mighty one of great splendor, the King of Righteousness, foremost of warriors, speaking to the grieving, drove away their sorrow.

sanskrit: yuddhe hy āśīviṣākārān rājaputrān raṇe bahūn pūrvaṃ nihatya saṃgrāme paścād ārjunir anvagāt
english: For in the battle the son of Arjuna, having first slain many princes who were like venomous serpents in the fight, followed after them in death at last.

sanskrit: hatvā daśasahasrāṇi kausalyaṃ ca mahāratham kṛṣṇārjunasamaḥ kārṣṇiḥ śakrasadma gato dhruvam
english: Having slain ten thousand warriors and the great car-warrior of Kosala, the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, equal to Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, has surely gone to the abode of Śakra.

sanskrit: rathāśvanaramātaṅgān vinihatya sahasraśaḥ avitṛptaḥ sa saṃgrāmād aśocyaḥ puṇyakarmakṛt
english: Having destroyed chariots, horses, men, and elephants by the thousand, unsated still of battle, he is not to be mourned, for he wrought deeds of merit.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu pravaraṃ hatvā teṣāṃ taiḥ śarapīḍitāḥ niveśāyābhyupāyāma sāyāhne rudhirokṣitāḥ
english: "But we, having slain the foremost of them, and ourselves tormented by their arrows, drew near to our camp at evening, drenched in blood."

sanskrit: nirīkṣamāṇās tu vayaṃ pare cāyodhanaṃ śanaiḥ apayātā mahārāja glāniṃ prāptā vicetasaḥ
english: "Gazing upon the battlefield, we and the foe alike withdrew slowly, O great king, overcome with weariness and bereft of our senses."

sanskrit: tato niśāyā divasasya cāśivaḥ; śivārutaḥ saṃdhir avartatādbhutaḥ kuśeśayāpīḍanibhe divākare; vilambamāne 'stam upetya parvatam
english: Then there came on, inauspicious and loud with the howling of jackals, the wondrous juncture of night and day, as the sun, like a chaplet of lotuses, lingered low and drew near the mountain of its setting.

sanskrit: varāsiśaktyṛṣṭivarūthacarmaṇāṃ; vibhūṣaṇānāṃ ca samākṣipan prabhām divaṃ ca bhūmiṃ ca samānayann iva; priyāṃ tanuṃ bhānur upaiti pāvakam
english: Stealing away the brightness of fine swords, spears, lances, chariot-guards, shields, and ornaments, and seeming to draw heaven and earth together as one, the sun went to embrace the fire, his beloved form.

sanskrit: mahābhrakūṭācalaśṛṅgasaṃnibhair; gajair anekair iva vajrapātitaiḥ savaijayantyaṅkuśavarmayantṛbhir; nipātitair niṣṭanatīva gauś citā
english: With many elephants resembling the peaks of great cloud-mountains, struck down as if by the thunderbolt—their pennons, goads, armor, and drivers with them—lying fallen, the earth seemed to groan, so heaped was she.

sanskrit: hateśvaraiś cūrṇitapattyupaskarair; hatāśvasūtair vipatākaketubhiḥ mahārathair bhūḥ śuśubhe vicūrṇitaiḥ; purair ivāmitrahatair narādhipa
english: With great chariots shattered to pieces—their lords slain, their footmen and gear ground to dust, their horses and drivers killed, their flags and standards gone—the earth shone, O ruler of men, like cities laid waste by the foe.

sanskrit: rathāśvavṛndaiḥ sahasādibhir hataiḥ; praviddhabhāṇḍābharaṇaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ nirastajihvādaśanāntralocanair; dharā babhau ghoravirūpadarśanā
english: With throngs of chariots and horses slain with their riders, their trappings and ornaments of every kind flung about, their tongues, teeth, entrails, and eyes torn out, the earth shone with an aspect dreadful and deformed.

sanskrit: praviddhavarmābharaṇā varāyudhā; vipannahastyaśvarathānugā narāḥ mahārhaśayyāstaraṇocitāḥ sadā; kṣitāv anāthā iva śerate hatāḥ
english: Men whose armor and ornaments were flung aside, whose fine weapons lay scattered, whose elephants, horses, chariots, and attendants had perished—men ever wonted to costly beds and coverlets—lay slain upon the ground, as though forlorn and masterless.
